title: Fixing double redemption of single-use coupons
hidden_flaw: An in-process mutex only serialises requests inside one Node.js process; the service runs 8 replicas (and each may run multiple workers), so the check-then-act race remains across instances. Needs an atomic DB-level operation (conditional UPDATE ... WHERE redeemed_at IS NULL RETURNING, unique constraint on redemptions, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE).
notes: Fundamental flaw: process-local lock for a cross-instance race.

input.objective: Stop single-use coupons from being redeemed twice when users double-click or retry checkout.
constraints: Checkout p99 must stay under 800 ms.
No new infrastructure components without platform-team approval.
input.context: coupon-service (Node.js 20, Express, Postgres 14 via Prisma). Redeem flow: `const c = await prisma.coupon.findUnique({where:{code}}); if (c.redeemedAt) throw Used; await chargeOrder(); await prisma.coupon.update({where:{code}, data:{redeemedAt: new Date(), orderId}})`. Finance found 312 double redemptions last month, clustered within 300 ms of each other, often from the same user on mobile with flaky networks (client retries).
input.proposed_solution: Wrap the redeem flow in an async mutex keyed by coupon code using the `async-mutex` package (a Map<code, Mutex>), so concurrent requests for the same code are serialised and the second one sees redeemedAt and fails. Add a unit test that fires two concurrent redeem calls and asserts only one succeeds. Low risk, ~30 lines, no schema change.
input.environment: Kubernetes, coupon-service runs 8 replicas behind a round-robin load balancer; clients retry on timeout after 2 s.
evidence: Duplicate redemptions: 312 in September; 71% had requests landing on different pods (by pod label in logs).
